senses.gloss:
Trika
(‘science of the three’)
------------------------------------------
Śaivism which primarily deals with three fundamentals—Pati (God), पशु (individual सोउल्) and पाश (bondage)—is generally called त्रिक also. It has three aspects: शैवागमस्, Spandaśāstra and Pratyabhijñāśāstra (or Kashmir शैविस्म्).
See ŚAIVĀGAMAS, SPANDA and Kashmir शैविस्म् under ŚAIVISM.

Triśikhabrāhmaṇopaniṣad
------------------------------------------
This Upaniṣad, though classed among the minor उपनिषद्स्, is fairly long.
Assigned to the Śukla Yajurveda, it is in two sections. The first one which is called Brāhmaṇabhāga, is in prose and has nine passages. The second one called Mantrabhāga, has 165 verses in the anuṣṭubh metre.
Since a greater part of the text deals with योग, it is included among the योग-उपनिषद्स्.
The first section deals with the process of च्रेअतिओन् from ब्रह्मन्, in a general way, as is found in other उपनिषद्स् and the Sāṅkhya system.
The topics delineated in the second section may be summarised as follows:
Four states of चोन्स्चिओउस्नेस्स्, तुरीय (the fourth) being the आत्मन्; the two paths देवयान (or उत्तरायण) and पितृयान (or दक्षिणायन); कर्मयोग as निष्कामकर्म (desireless action); aṣṭāṅgayoga or योग of eight limbs (described from the standpoint of Advaita Vedānta); some aspects of हठयोग such as यम, नियम प्राणायाम, nāḍīs and कुण्डलिनी; meditation on वासुदेव as परमात्मन् and मुक्ति or लिबेरतिओन्.

tripuṇḍra
(‘three [lines] as a religious mark’)
------------------------------------------
See TIRYAKPUṆḌRA and ŪRDHVAPUṆḌRA.

Trivikrama
(‘one with three steps’)
------------------------------------------
Even the Ṛgveda (1.22.17) refers to the त्रिविक्रम-अवतार of विष्णु.
See DAŚĀVATĀRAS for details.

Tripurabhairavī
(‘[the मोथेर्-goddess who is] fierce towards the three realms’)
------------------------------------------
She is one of the major forms of the मोथेर् goddess worshipped in her fierce as well as benevolent aspects.
Tripura signifies the three worlds—bhū (the earth), bhuvaḥ (the middle region) and suvaḥ (the हेअवेन्)—which she, in her fierce aspect, destroys at the end of a cycle of च्रेअतिओन्. It stands for धर्म (virtue), अर्थ (wealth) and काम (pleasure) in her benevolent aspect.
Iconographical works describe her thus: In her benevolent form, she is very bright like a thousand rising suns. She wears reddish silken garments. She has four arms, carrying in her two hands a book and a rosary while the other two exhibit the postures of boon-giving (varadamudrā) and protection (abhayamudrā).
In her fierce aspect she is shown as red in colour, with parted lips revealing blood-shot teeth and the eyes wild with intoxication. She wears garlands of skulls or a garland of three heads (of ब्रह्मा, विष्णु and रुद्र)!
In both these aspects she has three eyes and four arms. She also has matted hair-braids tied up into a topknot and adorned with a crescent मोओन्.

Trijaṭā
------------------------------------------
She was an old rākṣasī or demoness appointed by रावण as the leader of the demonesses who were guarding सीता in the अशोकवन (grove) in लङ्का. When she found the rākṣasīs harassing सीता, she advised them to desist from doing so since she had had a prophetic dream in which she had seen राम killing रावण in a battle (vide Rāmāyaṇa, Sundarakāṇḍa, sarga 27).
Trijaṭa is the name of an old ब्राह्मण who approached Śrī राम before his banishment, for wealth, and got it (Ayodhyākāṇḍa 32).

Tripurārṇava Tantra
------------------------------------------
This is considered as an important work of the tantra-group. It is stated to be a condensed version of a much bigger original work. It has 1636 ślokas or verses spread over 21 taraṅgas or chapters and is in the form of a dialogue between the देवी (Pārvatī) and ईश्वर or शिव.
A brief synopsis of the contents of the work may now be attempted here:
Taraṅga 1 (211 ślokas)
This taraṅga deals with the details connected with Tripurādīkṣā such as the qualities of the गुरु and the disciple, settling the date and time considered as auspicious, worship of the श्रीचक्र, होम, imparting the pañcadaśākṣarī मन्त्र (see मन्त्र">PAÑCADAŚĀKṢARĪ MANTRA and ŚRĪVIDYĀ.) and pūrṇābhiṣeka (final ritual bath).
Taraṅga 2 (105 ślokas)
This section delineates the topics like षट्चक्रभेद (See CAKRAS.), four types of प्राणायाम, method of ajapājapa (See जप">AJAPĀJAPA.) and some aspects of worship.
Taraṅga 3 (147 ślokas)
This chapter starts with the rites connected with the entering of the pūjāmandira or the main shrine. It is then followed by the descriptions of the details of पूजा or worship.
Nyāsas (ritual purification of limbs) connected with the षोडशी and the pañcadaśākṣarī mantras (See ŚRĪVIDYĀ.) as also other nyāsas are described next.
Taraṅga 4 (90 ślokas)
Drawing of the श्रीचक्र on metal plates of gold, silver and certain other materials is described here. Worship of शिव-śālagrama and liṅgas got in the नर्मदा river is highly beneficial and hence eulogised.
Taraṅga 5 (32 ślokas)
This section is mainly concerned with pīṭhapūjā or the worship of the small table on which the श्रीचक्र is kept. Several deities are established ceremonially on it with the appropriate mantras.
Taraṅga 6 (60 ślokas)
This chapter describes the आवाहन or inviting and instilling the goddess in the श्रीचक्र. Three types of pūjā—parā, aparā and miśra—are also stated.
Taraṅga 7 (36 ślokas)
Worship of two cakras—Sarvāśā-paripūraṇa and Sarvsaṁkṣobhaṇa—is set out here. They are two of the nine चक्रस् or yantras of the श्रीचक्र.
Taraṅga 8 (36 ślokas)
This taraṅga gives the details of the worship of the deities like गणेश, the नवग्रहस्, nakṣatras (asterisms), goddesses like the ḍākinīs and योगिनीस्, as also कामेश्वरी, Bhagamālinī, Vajreśvarī and Mahātripurasundarī.
Taraṅga 9 (48 ślokas)
The topics discussed here are: establishment of the vessels for arghya—both सामान्य (general) and viśeṣa (special)—, for कलश as also the metals to be used in their preparation. Related rites are also described.
Taraṅga 10 (65 ślokas)
This section deals mainly with the पञ्चमकारस् or the five M’s (See under TANTRAS.).
Taraṅga 11 (57 ślokas)
Various kalās (aspects of मोथेर् goddess in a minor form) grouped under Agnikalā, Sūryakalā and Somakalā, are described here.
Taraṅga 12 (32 ślokas)
Pūjā (ritualistic worship) and होम (worship through fire) of various kinds are the subject matter here.
Taraṅga 13 (69 ślokas)
This taraṅga deals with the final stages of पूजा and disposal of things connected with it.
Taraṅga 14 (103 ślokas)
This section contains many details connected with the kaulamārga or kaulācāra—the left handed path of tantras—such as maṇḍalapraveśa (entering the sacred spot), पूजा to elders like one’s गुरु, four kinds of sādhakas—uttama, madhyama, adhama and adhamādhama—continuous practice of the disciplines taught, condemnation of religious सुइचिदे, deep faith in the गुरु and the śāstras and so on.
Taraṅga 15 (47 ślokas)
Mudrās or poses of fingers and hands are the subject matter here.
Thirteen mudras, to be shown before ललिता-त्रिपुरसुन्दरी are described in detail. Some of them are: saṅkṣobhiṇī, vidrāviṇī, ākarṣaṇī, vaśaṅkarī, pāśamudrā, aṅkuśamudrā and so on.
Some other mudrās used in pūjā—like धेनुमुद्रा or tārkṣyamudrā—are also given.
Taraṅga 16 (20 ślokas)
Shortened forms of पूजा are prescribed here for the benefit of those who are unable to do the whole पूजा due to various factors including lack of intelligence.
Taraṅga 17 (61 ślokas)
Pūjā is of two kinds: नित्य (daily) and naimittika (occasional). Those who cannot do the first, can take recourse to the second. It may be done once a month or once in six months. In extreme cases, it may be got done through the गुरु or anyone else. This, as also some other special pūjās to be done during नवरात्र, are described here.
Taraṅga 18 (76 ślokas)
This taraṅga is mainly devoted to the exposition of the famous Khaḍga-mālāstotra. First, the preliminaries like ṛṣi (sage), छन्दस् (metre), devatā (the deity) and viniyoga (utility) are stated. Though the original hymn is in a long metre, दण्डक by name, here the same is stated in the anuṣṭubh or śloka metre.
The Khaḍgamālā hymn has several names of the goddess. The methods of using them in पूजा, होम and तर्पण (oblations of water) are also indicated.
Taraṅga 19 (243 ślokas)
This section starts with a detailed description of the Rahoyāga, a याग to देवी to be done in seclusion. It can be performed only by those who are initiated into the worship of the देवी. The benefits that accrue to its performer as also the methods of remedying the defects that might have crept in during the performance are also described.
Taraṅga 20 (80 ślokas)
This section gives the mantras of the Atharvaveda used in the Rahoyāga. This is followed by a description of the पूजा to श्रीचक्र with the mantras of the well-known Śrīsūkta.
It ends with mentioning the various fruits or results of using different materials like बिल्व leaves or flowers or cereals in होम.
Taraṅga 21 (18 ślokas)
This last taraṅga states the different fruits that a person can get by the recitation of the Śrīsūkta, which has also been called Tripurāsūkta here.

Tristhalī
(‘the three [great] places [of पिल्ग्रिमगे]’)
------------------------------------------
Of all the Hindu places of पिल्ग्रिमगे, प्रयाग (the modern Allahabad in the Uttar Pradesh State), काशी (Vārāṇasī, the modern Banaras, also in Uttar Pradesh) and गया (in Bihar) are considered the most ancient and holy. These three together are called त्रिस्थली.
Nārāyaṇabhaṭṭa (A. D. 1513) a well-known author of धर्मशास्त्रस् has written an authoritative and voluminous work called Tristhalīsetu. It might have been composed around A. D. 1580 in Banaras.

Trisuparṇamantras
(‘the mantras that guard like the सुपर्ण [Garuḍa]’)
------------------------------------------
The ten mantras of the three anuvākas (sections)—38, 39 and 40—of the Mahānārāyaṇopaniṣad are collectively known as Trisuparṇamantras. This has been declared in the Upaniṣad itself.
As सुपर्ण or गरुड (the eagle-mount of Lord विष्णु) protects अमृत or nectar, these mantras when recited will protect a seeker of spiritual wisdom from the evil effects of even heinous sins like ब्रह्महत्या (killing a ब्राह्मण). Hence they are called Suparṇamantras. Since they are spread over three (= tri) anu-vākas, they are called Trisuparṇamantras.
A brief summary of these mantras may now be given:
Anuvāka 38
May ब्रह्मन्, the blissful Lord, come to me. O Lord! I am your child. Destroy my bad dream of सṁसार (empirical existence). I offer myself as an oblation into Thee.
These Trisuparṇamantras should be given to any ब्राह्मण, even if unsolicited. Those who recite them, destroy the sin of ब्रह्महत्या or killing a ब्राह्मण. They become so pure that they can purify a thousand ब्राह्मणस्, while sitting for ड़ोओद्, in the same row.
Anuvāka 39
Brahman who is bliss is attained through the power of intelligence.
O God the Creator! give us prosperity consisting of progeny. Turn away from us this bad dream of the world.
Turn away from us all sins and bring to us what is auspicious.
May the whole nature consisting of wind, rivers, vegetation, night and dawn, particles of earth and sun, be sweet to us.
Anuvāka 40
The (Supreme) ब्रह्मन् is attained only by a person in whom the desire for Self-knowledge is generated by the proper performance of prescribed duties.
It is the Supreme Being who has become the best in everything: ब्रह्मा (the four-faced creator) among the gods; master of right words among the composers; the seer among the intelligent beings; the strong buffalo among the animals; the kite among the birds; the axe among the destructive tools and सोम juice that is praised, among the sacrificers.
It is He again who is in the sun, in the air, in the fire, as also in the individual सोउल्.

Trita
------------------------------------------
The sage गौतम had three sons known as Ekata, Dvita and त्रित.
Once these three brothers went to a sacrifice, participated as priests and got money. त्रित got more than his brothers since he was more competent. While returning home, the two elder brothers pushed त्रित into a well and ran away with his wealth. त्रित prayed to the विश्वेदेवस् (or Aśvinīdevatās) and got out through their grace. He also cursed his brothers to become wolves!
According to another version (vide Skandasvāmi’s commentary on Ṛgveda 1.105.1) त्रित fell into a well when pursued by wolves. There, he saw a creeper, imagined it to be the सोम creeper and mentally performed a सोम sacrifice. Various gods, along with बृहस्पति (their preceptor), appeared before him, granted him all the boons he asked for and also rescued him.
The Ṛgveda, in another place vide 8.47.15) mentions that त्रित-Āptya prayed to gods to be freed from the effects of bad द्रेअम्स्. Hence this मन्त्र may be repeated as a sacred formula to ward off evil द्रेअम्स्.

Trimūrti
(‘Trinity’)
------------------------------------------
Brahman—God the Absolute—creates the world, sustains it and withdraws it back into Himself (vide Brahmasūtras 1.1.2). In paurāṇic हिन्दुइस्म् this ब्रह्मन् is described as three deities: ब्रह्मा responsible for च्रेअतिओन्; विष्णु responsible for its sustenance; and, रुद्र or शिव responsible for its destruction at the end of a cosmic cycle. These three deities correspond to the three guṇas (rajas, सत्त्व and तमस्) in the cosmic play of च्रेअतिओन्, sustenance and destruction.
They are the Trimūrtis (or the Hindu Trinity).
There are composite images in which all the three gods are represented, like दत्तात्रेय.
See DATTĀTREYA.

Triśaṅku
(‘one who had committed three śaṅkus or sins’)
------------------------------------------
There can be no better example for human frailty than that of त्रिशङ्कु (a king of the इक्ष्वाकु race), who happened to be the ड़थेर् of हरिश्चन्द्र, the redoubtable champion of सत्य or truth. That his ड़थेर् Nibandhana had christened him ‘Satyavrata’ (= one who follows truth religiously) might be construed as adding insult to injury!
Since the prince Satyavrata had committed three śaṅkus or sins—adultery, killing a cow and eating its flesh—he came to be known as त्रिशङ्कु.
Once he decided to perform a sacrifice that would enable him to go to स्वर्ग (heaven), keeping his physical body intact. The well-known sage विश्वामित्र agreed to do it for him. However, the gods in हेअवेन् refused to come and accept his offerings. Incensed by this, विश्वामित्र started sending त्रिशङ्कु to स्वर्ग, by the power of his तपस् or austerities. When Satyavrata was halfway through his upward journey, he was cursed by इन्द्र to fall on earth, upside down. विश्वामित्र came to his rescue again by stopping him in the middle of the sky and started creating a separate हेअवेन् for his sake! Alarmed by this, the gods of हेअवेन् under इन्द्र’s leadership pleaded with the sage that त्रिशङ्कु, because of his threefold sin, was unfit to enter हेअवेन्. As a compromise it was agreed that त्रिशङ्कु would stay where he was, surrounded by his own world of स्तर्स्.
Triśaṅku-स्वर्ग has now become a byword for anything which is ‘neither here, nor there’ (vide Rāmāyaṇa, Bālakāṇḍa 57 and 60).

trivṛtkaraṇa
(‘the process of triplication’)
------------------------------------------
The Chāndogya Upaniṣad (6.2.3,4; 6.3.3) mentions that ब्रह्मन् (called ‘Sat’ here) created three fundamental elements out of himself. They are: तेजस् (fire), āpa (water) and अन्न (earth).
These three are the pure elements imperceptible to the senses.
Brahman then created the gross elements out of these, by the process of त्रिवृत्करण or triplication. In this, half of one subtle or sūkṣma element is combined with one-fourth of the other two, resulting in the gross (sthūla) element as follows:
(subtle) तेजस् ½ + (subtle) āpa ¼ + (subtle) अन्न ¼ = gross or sthūla तेजस्.
This is technically called त्रिवृत्करण.
The process is similar to that of पञ्चीकरण.
See PAÑCĪKARAṆA.

triguṇātīta
(‘one who has transcended the three guṇas’)
------------------------------------------
See GUṆĀTĪTA.

triśūla
(‘trident’)
------------------------------------------
Also called triśikhā (triple flame) and triśīrṣaka (three-headed), it is the trident (a weapon) normally shown in the hand of शिव and some aspects of the देवी (the Divine मोथेर्).
Viśvakarma the divine architect, is said to have fashioned it out of a portion of the तेजस् of the Sun (solar disc). The सुदर्शनचक्र (discus) of विष्णु, the शक्ति (spear) of सुब्रह्मण्य as also the Puṣpakavimāna (divine flying machine) of कुबेर were also prepared by him from the same solar disc (vide Viṣṇupurāṇa 3.2.10, 11).
